causal-factors.name: Definitive death of Ali Khamenei (Feb 28, 2026) confirmed by multiple outlets
causal-factors.rationale: The death directly ends his tenure and triggers Iran's formal succession process, as reported by AP, Washington Post, Guardian, and Time.

causal-factors.name: Prediction-market pre-event odds of departure within 2026

causal-factors.name: Constitutional mechanism to appoint a new Supreme Leader (Assembly of Experts, Article 111)
causal-factors.rationale: Iran's constitution requires the Assembly of Experts to appoint a replacement in the shortest possible time after death, driving a rapid transition.

causal-factors.name: Temporary governance arrangement during vacancy
causal-factors.rationale: Article 111 contemplates a temporary council to oversee duties during the interim, mitigating prolonged vacancy.

causal-factors.name: Uncertainty about the identity of the successor
causal-factors.rationale: No immediate, publicly named designated successor appears, leaving post-transition leadership dynamics open.

causal-factors.name: Risk of misinformation or retractions
causal-factors.rationale: Although initial reports are corroborated, the possibility of later retractions exists but is unlikely given multiple independent sources.

causal-factors.name: Death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei confirmed by credible outlets
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple credible sources (AP, Washington Post, The Guardian) reported Khamenei's death on Feb 28–29, 2026, making cessation before April 1, 2026 effectively certain.

causal-factors.name: Activation of Iran's Assembly of Experts succession mechanism
causal-factors.rationale: Iran's constitutional process for selecting a new Supreme Leader is now in play, providing a formal path to leadership transition and reducing post-event uncertainty.

causal-factors.name: Uncertainty about the identity and timing of the successor
causal-factors.rationale: While the death triggers a transition, the ultimate successor and the speed of consolidation remain unclear, introducing some governance uncertainty even as the event has occurred.

synthesis: Credible outlets confirmed Khamenei's death on Feb 28, 2026, ending his tenure and triggering Iran's succession process. With strong pre-existing market odds and formal constitutional mechanisms, cessation before April 1, 2026 is highly likely; remaining uncertainty concerns the exact successor, not the occurrence of cessation.
